newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Bank Hapoalim EPS raised.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Bank Hapoalim EPS raised.

text.p: Sahar Securities & Investments raised its 1997 earnings per share (EPS) estimate for Bank Hapoalim after the Israeli bank reported better than expected first quarter results.
Sahar raised its 1997 EPS estimate to 0.85 shekels from a previous estimate of 0.73. Last year Israel's largest bank earned 0.68 shekels a share.
"Bank Hapoalim's first quarter results exceeded our expectations and may definitely be characterised as a pleasant surprise," Sahar analyst Doron Tsur said in a report.

"The bulk of the difference originates from a provision for doubtful debt that is considerably lower than we forecasted as well as less severe damage than we anticipated as a result of the weakening Swiss franc," the report said.

Tsur raised his target share price for the end of the year to 9.4 to 10.2 shekels from a previous target of 8.5 shekels. He also maintained his buy recommendation for the shares, which are trading at 7.91 shekels.
